Subject: Proposal: capacity top-up timing & discount structure

Hi Cara —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Per our conversation, I pulled together two practical paths to handle LuminaHealth's mid-contract growth so you can pick whichever fits procurement and internal budgeting best. TL;DR: we can either (A) a staged top-up that keeps your current co-term and spreads billing across two invoices, or (B) an annualize-and-credit option that moves the new capacity onto an annualized co-term today with an upfront credit to offset unused committed capacity.

Option A — Staged top-up (no co-term change)- Add 25% interim capacity now- Bill prorated for the remainder of the term on next invoice + full rates going forward- No retroactive changes to commit level

Option B — Annualize & credit (co-term to next renewal)- Add full requested uplift immediately and annualize to your renewal date- We apply a one-time credit equal to the unused portion of your existing commit (per attached usage report)- Provides predictable unit price and simplifies reporting

Attached: Lumina_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (draft pricing and credit math) and usage_report_q3.csv for line-by-line justification.

Ben can outline the exact dollar math; Priya is on hand for billing cutovers. If you prefer, we can also propose a blended hybrid with a smaller upfront annualization + staged remainder.

Next steps: please tell us which option your procurement team prefers and whether you need the uplift invoiced to your existing PO or a new one. Happy to schedule a 30-minute call with finance if helpful.

Best,
Mina

Hi Cara — nice to e-meet. Answers below, plus a concrete worksheet excerpt.

1) Credit presentation: we can do either. Most customers prefer a single invoice with a negative credit line for visibility; if your AP requires a separate credit memo we can produce that as well. No accounting difference for you.

2) Overages: under Option B (annualize) any usage above the uplift will be billed at the annualized unit price (i.e., the discounted unit) until the renewal date. This is a common ask for customers who need predictable unit economics during a ramp.

3) One-page change summary: attached to this reply (see below) — it lists the specific SOW lines that change, effective dates, and the credit calculation. Legal can attach it as an addendum.

Q: delaying effective date to Jan 1 — yes, that shifts the credit slightly because fewer days of the existing commit remain to be credited; rough estimate shows ~6% smaller credit if moved to Jan 1 versus Nov 22. We can provide exact numbers if you confirm the date.

Attached: Lumina_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (updated with a one-page summary).

If tomorrow 10:00 PT works, Mina and I will join + Priya for billing details. If procurement still prefers asynchronous, share the preferred PO flow and we'll send a final amendment + invoice plan.
